The code already separates a vendor-neutral `TaxPreparation::TaxAutomations` core from provider-specific namespaces. **Instead is the only registered adapter today.** `gruntworx` already has a provider enum value, but that does not register an integration. Juno still uses its older implementation outside the adapter registry.

**Vendor-neutral ports**

The core owns the application-facing operations and shared rules:

| Area | Core responsibilities |
|---|---|
| Authorization and connection | Start authorization; complete connection; read, disconnect, renew and revoke grants; verify refused grants. |
| Export | Authorize access, validate documents against provider capabilities, maintain the tax-return envelope and send records, then dispatch to the adapter. |
| Status and recovery | Apply unified processing statuses, broadcast changes, resume sends stopped by authorization failure, and schedule reconciliation. |
| CRM and firm lifecycle | Supply export-form prefills, merge contact records, remove envelopes and clean up provider data on firm deletion. |
| Infrastructure | Shared HTTP/OAuth client, connection state machine, signed OAuth state, presigned byte transfer, metrics and async-operation infrastructure. |

The main export port passes **core records**, rather than a vendor-shaped payload, to `adapter::ExportAsync`. Instead then starts its own export workflow after the enclosing transaction commits. Vendor API sequencing remains inside the adapter.

Sources: [core export](/Users/Shared/nav-ab/repo-master/app/services/tax_preparation/tax_automations/export_async.rb:53), [Instead export](/Users/Shared/nav-ab/repo-master/app/services/tax_preparation/tax_automations/instead/export_async.rb:28), [status-update port](/Users/Shared/nav-ab/repo-master/app/services/tax_preparation/tax_automations/documents/update_status.rb:3).

**Registration and the adapter contract**

Registration is a static mapping:

```ruby
ADAPTERS = { instead: TaxPreparation::TaxAutomations::Instead }.freeze
FEATURE_FLAGS = { instead: :tax_automations_instead }.freeze
```

`Registry.adapter_for(firm)` reads the provider from `FirmSettings`; `adapter_for_provider(provider)` resolves an explicit provider and raises `UnknownProviderError` if it is unregistered. Explicit resolution matters during provider switching and when processing historical sends. A provider without a feature-flag entry is offered to every firm.

The required namespace contract comes from production dispatch sites, including background workers. Below, `u, a` means user and actor:

| Required namespace member | Invocation or responsibility |
|---|---|
| `Connection` | ActiveRecord model with `.for_firm(firm)`, `.usable_for(firm)`, `.capabilities`, grant states, token storage and normal lookup/scoping methods. |
| `Client` | `.new(connection)`; shared OAuth operations `renew!` and `revoke_tokens!`; signed-target upload where used. |
| `Authorizations::Create` | `.call(u, a, provider, return_url)` → authorization URL. |
| `Connections::Create` | `.call(u, a, provider, params)` → connection after completing authorization. |
| `ExportAsync` | `.call(u, a, tax_preparation, tax_automation_documents: records)` → starts provider work. |
| `Documents::ReconcileStatusesAsync` | `.call(u, a, connection, tax_automation_document_ids: ids)` → schedules status reconciliation. |
| `DestroyForTaxPreparations` | `.call(u, a, firm_id, tax_preparations)` → removes provider records associated with those envelopes. |
| `DestroyForFirm` | `.call(u, a, firm_id)` → removes the firm’s provider data. |
| `MergeForContact` | `.call(u, a, firm_id, source_contact_id, target_contact_id)` → merges provider-side contact associations. |

These services use the existing service-result convention: callers inspect success/failure, errors and data. Cleanup and keep-alive iterate **all registered adapters**, so implementing only authorization and export would leave the contract incomplete.

Sources: [registry](/Users/Shared/nav-ab/repo-master/app/lib/tax_preparation/tax_automations/registry.rb:3), [reconciliation dispatch](/Users/Shared/nav-ab/repo-master/app/workers/tax_preparation/tax_automations/documents/reconcile_sweep_worker.rb:34), [firm cleanup](/Users/Shared/nav-ab/repo-master/app/services/tax_preparation/tax_automations/firms/destroy_cleanup.rb:55), [envelope cleanup](/Users/Shared/nav-ab/repo-master/app/services/tax_preparation/tax_automations/tax_preparations/batch_destroy.rb:50), [contact merge](/Users/Shared/nav-ab/repo-master/app/services/tax_preparation/tax_automations/tax_preparations/merge_for_contact.rb:92).

The existing extension mechanism is **OAuth-oriented**. `HasOauthConnection` supplies encrypted credentials, expiry handling and the common lifecycle:

- `disconnected`, `connected`, `expired`, `revoked`.
- Both connected and expired grants can be usable, because refresh may recover an expired grant.
- Disconnect retains credentials until withdrawal is attempted; revoke drops them.
- `BaseClient` includes `TokenRefreshable`. A subclass supplies `base_url`, `auth_headers` and `vendor_error_message`, and declares OAuth endpoint/settings information. Vendor-specific error classification and grant identity extraction are optional hooks.

This is a material constraint when assessing how GruntWorx would fit the current architecture.

Sources: [connection contract](/Users/Shared/nav-ab/repo-master/app/models/concerns/tax_preparation/tax_automations/has_oauth_connection.rb:22), [client hooks](/Users/Shared/nav-ab/repo-master/app/lib/tax_preparation/tax_automations/base_client.rb:459), [OAuth configuration](/Users/Shared/nav-ab/repo-master/app/lib/tax_preparation/tax_automations/token_refreshable.rb:63).

**The capability passport**

The passport is a typed `Dry::Struct` returned by `Connection.capabilities`. It describes the **provider**, so constructing it requires no connection row.

Its shape is:

```text
Capabilities
  terms[]
    return_type
    accepted_file_formats[]
    max_file_size_mb
  supported_tax_years[]
```

Formats and size limits are specified **per return type**. Supported return types are derived from `terms`; `passport.for(code)` returns that form’s terms or `nil` when unsupported.

The adapter supplies private class methods `capability_terms` and `supported_tax_years`. Construction validates formats, positive integer size limits, duplicate return-type declarations and years from 2000 through the current year plus one. Validation is lazy: missing implementations or malformed values fail when `.capabilities` is called.

The passport serves two consumers:

- Export validation checks return type, year, extension and file size.
- The API serializer presents `tax_years` and enriched `return_types`, including code, display name, personal/business family, `file_types` and `file_size_limit`.

Instead currently declares all eleven mapped return types, shares configured file terms across them, and supports the current calendar year plus the preceding two years.

Sources: [passport definition](/Users/Shared/nav-ab/repo-master/app/models/tax_preparation/tax_automations/has_capabilities.rb:19), [validation](/Users/Shared/nav-ab/repo-master/app/services/tax_preparation/tax_automations/export/validate_documents.rb:40), [API representation](/Users/Shared/nav-ab/repo-master/app/serializers/tax_preparation/base/tax_automations/connection_serializer.rb:57), [Instead declarations](/Users/Shared/nav-ab/repo-master/app/models/tax_preparation/tax_automations/instead/connection.rb:69).

**Data model**

| Entity | Ownership and relationships |
|---|---|
| `FirmSettings` | One per firm. Stores the selected provider and external tenant/account binding. Provider enum: `juno: 0`, `gruntworx: 1`, `instead: 2`. |
| Core `TaxPreparation` | Tax-return envelope addressed by firm, CRM client, optional contact and year; carries return type, EIN and business name. Still physically stored in `juno_tax_preparations`. Legacy Juno associations coexist with core addressing. |
| Core `Document` | Send junction linking an existing TaxDome document to an envelope, provider and return type. Unique on `(firm_id, tax_preparation_id, document_id, provider, return_type)`. Provider and return type preserve the send’s identity even when current settings change. |
| Instead `Connection` | One grant per firm; polymorphic staff creator (`Owner` or `Employee`), encrypted tokens, expiries and lifecycle timestamps. |
| Instead `Entity` | Vendor taxpayer identity associated with client/contact and entity type, carrying an external UUID and vendor snapshot/archive information. |
| Instead `Document` | Vendor-specific extension of one core send record: entity link, upload path and external file UUID. |

The core send record owns two separate state machines:

- Upload: `waiting → uploading → uploaded`, with failure and reset paths.
- Processing: `sent`, `processing`, `processed`, `error`, `archived`, `exceeded`.

A shared `failure_reason` vocabulary records failures. Provider adapters translate vendor statuses into that vocabulary.

On a provider switch, settings change only when the new connection completes successfully. Historical send records retain their provider, and old provider records remain reachable for cleanup.

Sources: [firm settings](/Users/Shared/nav-ab/repo-master/app/models/tax_preparation/tax_automations/firm_settings.rb:5), [envelope](/Users/Shared/nav-ab/repo-master/app/models/tax_preparation/tax_automations/tax_preparation.rb:3), [send record and states](/Users/Shared/nav-ab/repo-master/app/models/tax_preparation/tax_automations/document.rb:3), [Instead entity](/Users/Shared/nav-ab/repo-master/app/models/tax_preparation/tax_automations/instead/entity.rb:3), [Instead document](/Users/Shared/nav-ab/repo-master/app/models/tax_preparation/tax_automations/instead/document.rb:3), [provider switching](/Users/Shared/nav-ab/repo-master/app/services/tax_preparation/tax_automations/connections/create.rb:42).
